title: alternatives
subtitle: Managed symlinks that pick which binary a public name points at — flip to reveal meaning, example, and notes

cards.meaning: Creates, removes, maintains, and displays the symbolic links that pick which implementation a public name (e.g. /usr/bin/java) points at
cards.notes: Memory hook: a managed symlink farm. One public name, many real binaries, one current choice. You do not delete the other versions.

cards.meaning: Debian/Ubuntu name for the same idea as Red Hat alternatives
cards.notes: This course uses the Red Hat command alternatives.

cards.meaning: Group name for this alternative set
Real binary that provides the group
Integer; in auto mode the highest priority wins
Extra symlinks that must switch with the master (man page, javac, …)
Register a new path in the group
cards.notes: Order: public link, group name, real path, priority (higher wins in --auto).

cards.meaning: Unregister that path from the group
Pin the group to a specific path (manual mode)
Show status, paths, priorities, and current choice
Interactive menu to pick a provider by number
cards.notes: Type a number to switch; Enter keeps the current selection.

cards.meaning: The one that would be chosen in auto mode (highest priority)
Confirm which JVM /usr/bin/java now is after switching
cards.notes: java on PATH is the symlink target you selected — not a second copy of the JVM. After --config, version must match the path you picked.

cards.meaning: --install to add, --config to pick by menu, --set to pick by path, --auto to follow priority, --display to inspect, --remove to drop
